`7bd67f5` edits `modules/tools/ssh-tpm-agent.nix`, imported directly by
`sweet16-home` and `petunia-home` and nothing else.

Expected: sweet16 and petunia drift; avina and hermes zero, since they import
neither the module nor `user-home`; standalone groot configurations unmoved.

Note this differs from the last two sign-offs, where all four NixOS hosts drifted
because `core-security` was involved. Nothing fleet-wide is touched here.

### Actual vs expected

Matches: sweet16 and petunia drift; avina, hermes, groot@dualie and groot@forge
byte-identical; groot@rk3588 N/A (aarch64).

### Why the sealed key was not moved

`~/.ssh/id_ecdsa` is in ssh's default identity list, so a canonical public-key
name means the key is offered with no client configuration — including under
`IdentitiesOnly`, which lists exactly those default paths and would otherwise
offer nothing. That was the failure mode against Gitea.

Only the public half is linked. Moving the sealed key was tested and rejected:
an agent run with `--key-dir ~/.ssh` picked up `~/.ssh/agents/` as well, loading
both the personal and agentic keys into one agent. That would collapse the two
sockets into one and give any permafrost guest the personal key for the life of
a forwarded connection — the precise property the split exists to prevent.

The certificate link runs the opposite way: renewals are written to the canonical
path, while ssh-tpm-agent reads certificates only from its own `--key-dir`. Both
targets are generated per host at runtime, so `mkOutOfStoreSymlink`.

### The cert-check defect

`ssh-keygen -L` prints the validity window in local time. The script parsed it
with `date -u -d`, treating it as UTC and understating remaining validity by the
UTC offset — four hours during EDT. A certificate with roughly eight hours left
was reported as expired by 188 minutes, which falsely blocked a fleet deploy at
the cert gate while sshd was accepting the same certificate without complaint.
Every reading taken this session was four hours low.

Fixed to `date -d`, and confirmed against an independent calculation: 477 minutes
remaining against an 8h TTL.

### Verified after deploying

With `IdentitiesOnly=yes` and no explicit `IdentityFile`, ssh resolves
`~/.ssh/id_ecdsa` to the public key, matches it against the agent, and offers
both the key and its certificate — `Authenticated to petunia.home.lan`. The
now-redundant `IdentityFile`/`IdentityAgent` lines were removed from the
hand-managed Gitea block and behaviour is unchanged.
